humanities_role_explanation: Linguistic and wordplay items (grammar, honorifics, puns, homophones, idioms) and cultural/tradition items (holidays, calendars, customs) test disciplinary-style linguistic/cultural competence, while the math-with-cultural-relevance items use cultural material as context for calculations, a general reasoning competence. Results are reported separately per category.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only questions in French, Spanish and Chinese, plus manually translated English equivalents for the cultural and math categories.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Four categories: language-specific linguistic reasoning (grammar rules, word formation, honorifics), wordplay and riddles (puns, homophones, Chengyu), cultural/tradition reasoning (timelines, holidays, customs, date computation), and math reasoning with cultural relevance (calendars, currencies, counting systems). Answers are short, free-text final answers checked against a ground-truth final answer (GTFA).

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to native multilingual reasoning in four categories and three languages, not a broad multi-task benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 14 model variants including o3-pro, o3, o4-mini, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude 4 Opus/Sonnet, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Deepseek-R1, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Llama-4-Maverick.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy (pass@1) judged by GPT-4.1 LLM judge, with 95% confidence intervals; Scott's Pi agreement with humans.

summary: The paper introduces MultiNRC, a benchmark of 1,055 native reasoning questions in French, Spanish and Chinese, written by native speakers and filtered so that at least 3 of 5 strong LLMs fail. It evaluates 14 LLMs, finding none above 50%, and compares performance against English-equivalent translations for the cultural and math categories.
key_findings: Best model o3-pro reaches 49.00% accuracy; no model exceeds 50%. Math is hardest (23.3% average). English equivalents raise math accuracy on average (+19.1 Spanish, +12.5 Chinese) but cultural reasoning shows negligible change. Spanish is the hardest language; average gap between best and worst language per model is 13.90 points.
facets_explanation: Native speakers wrote each prompt and a short ground-truth final answer, then two native-speaker reviewer layers verified answer accuracy, category alignment and the 3-of-5 model failure criterion. The annotators are native speakers rather than documented disciplinary experts, so domain_expert is the closest label. Questions are language- and culture-specific, requiring local knowledge not in the prompt. An LLM judge compares model output to the GTFA.
results_explanation: Table 3: 'o3-pro-2025-06-10-high 49.00 (±3.02)' is the best Original accuracy. Table 5 average math delta for Spanish is 19.1 (English minus Original), the largest reported gap. Spanish is 'the most challenging language across categories'. No human performance baseline is reported; only judge-human agreement is given.
